quickSummary: Chiral centers are sp³ carbons with 4 different groups. Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images; diastereomers are non-mirror stereoisomers. Specific rotation [α]_λ^T = α / (l · c). Racemic mixtures are equimolar (1:1) and optically inactive (α=0). S_N2 gives 100% inversion; S_N1 gives racemization with partial inversion.
summary: Master chirality, optical activity calculations, enantiomeric excess, and stereochemical outcomes in nucleophilic substitutions.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Polarimetry & Specific Rotation ($[\alpha]_\lambda^T$): The rotation of plane-polarized light passing through an optically active solution is quantified by:
$$\mathbf{[\alpha]_\lambda^T = \frac{\alpha}{l \cdot c}}$$
where $\alpha$ is the observed optical rotation in degrees, $l$ is the sample cell path length in decimeters ($\text{dm}$), and $c$ is the concentration in $\text{g/mL}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 Stereochemical Outcomes in Substitution Reactions
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Stereochemical Outcomes in Substitution Reactions
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
STEREOCHEMICAL OUTCOMES
                      
   RETENTION:    Nucleophile attaches at the EXACT SAME spatial position as the leaving group.
   INVERSION:    Nucleophile attaches at the OPPOSITE face relative to the leaving group ($S_N2$).
   RACEMIZATION: Formation of an equimolar $50:50$ mixture of retained and inverted enantiomers ($S_N1$).

Enantiomeric Excess (ee):
ee = (Observed Rotation / Pure Enantiomer Rotation) × 100
% S_N2 = % Net Inversion = ee
% S_N1 = 100% - % S_N2
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Retention**: Nucleophile enters the identical spatial position.
- **Inversion**: Backside attack causes umbrella-like inversion ($S_N2$).
- **Racemization**: Planar carbocation attacked equally from both faces ($S_N1$).

quickRevision: Chiral center: sp³ carbon with 4 different groups.
Enantiomers have equal and opposite optical rotations (±α).
Racemic mixture: 1:1 mixture of enantiomers, optically inactive (α=0).
Enantiomeric excess: ee = (Observed / Pure) × 100 = % S_N2 net inversion.
